reported.title: No hysteresis or filtering causes fan relay chatter
reported.description: The control logic at lines 72-79 opens the fan at >=28.0 C but closes it for any value below 28.0 C, with no 24.0 C close threshold and no input filtering. Sensor noise near the threshold therefore flips D9 on every 50 ms tick; measured evidence shows 46 toggles in a 5000 ms window (limit 2) in the threshold-hover scenario and 12 toggles in the hysteresis-collapse scenario. D9 toggled 12 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 50 ms (limit 2), and 21 times over the whole 12.00 s run.

reported.title: Fault range (below 5 C / above 100 C / floating) not forced to safe ON
reported.description: The firmware never checks for out-of-range or floating probe readings; lines 72-79 simply treat any temperature below 28.0 C as a command to turn the fan off. A 3.0 C reading or a disconnected 0 V probe thus drives D9 LOW instead of forcing it HIGH, and the measured evidence shows D9 not in safe state HIGH for 5400 ms during the disconnected-sensor fault (allowed 600 ms). During the fault, D9 was not in safe state HIGH for 920 ms (allowed 600 ms to react).

judge_input.spec:
- LM35 greenhouse air probe on A2 at 10 mV/°C; exhaust fan relay on D9.
- Open the fan when temperature reaches 28.0 °C or above; close the fan when temperature falls to 24.0 °C or below.
- Fan must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- If the probe is floating, or temperature reads below 5.0 °C or above 100.0 °C, force the fan ON within 600 ms and hold that safe state for the duration of the fault.
- Print `gh: <temp> C fan=ON` or `gh: <temp> C fan=OFF` every 1000 ms with temperature to one decimal place.
- Reach the commanded fan state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.
